status: Seven exact original-source point proposals independently approved; five inspected notes retained. Root applies separately.
scope: Twelve fresh remaining BEL chapter1 lower-vowel targets outside the Pass8 ten: mem8/28/29/38, bet19/27/33/40/41, kaf1 and shin/sin33. Lower Theodotion body only. This is not an all216-note review.
method: Literal exact same-font positive and competing point classes compared against full target glyphs and complete words. Source-native crops and integer nearest-neighbor enlargements only. Four original A2 page rasters were freshly reextracted from the PDF and shown pixel-identical to the existing native PNGs. Every durable crop/enlargement was freshly replayed; an independent peer also replayed all seven target/word addresses directly from the PDF. No OCR, grammar/expected spelling, sharpening, filtering, contrast changes, interpolation or upper Septuagint substitution. Incorrect exploratory control crops were discarded before decisions. The bet33 close frame was extended downward to expose its complete point; no source pixels reconstructed.
canonicalApplicationState: No canonical, central-review, daily-reading, generated, browser-session or saved-PDF mutations by this report author. Other shared-word notes require only the enumerated anchor refreshes.

observations.finding: The lower mark is a flatter smeared bar with multiple foot connections. Its reduced lobe structure does not securely distinguish a flat bar from a fully coalesced pair; retain after comparison against mem patah/tsere controls.

Two low rounded nodes around a small central window/valley under the mem match literal same-font mem tsere. The shape differs from the flat patah bar, deep central qamats stem and third lower segol node.

Two rounded lower tips with a distinct central lower valley and a white window repeat the same-font mem tsere contour. Patah, qamats and three-node segol controls preserve materially different lower shapes.

The lower mem mark has two upper rounded lobes and a third central lower node through a short neck, matching the exact same-page mem segol in והמלך. The qamats counterexample instead has a much longer thin descending stem. Numbered original lower-recension context verifies the target word before the following printed39 דניאל line.

The bet has two rounded low tips around a central white window, matching the literal bet tsere in הבל. Qamats and segol bets in בבל have respectively a long thin lower stem/button and a third central lower point, absent from this target.

A fresh correctly centered whole-bet frame replaces an earlier close view emphasizing neighboring shin/yod. The broad filled lower foot has no uniquely recoverable stamp or bar arrangement. Plain-bet controls show that a flat basal edge can be ordinary letter anatomy; neither a vowel class nor its absence is certified.

The expanded target frame exposes the full long narrow descending stem and lower button beneath the fused bet foot/shoulder, clear of the next row. This matches the literal first-bet qamats in בבל; the second-bet segol has three shorter-spaced nodes and the bet tsere has two low tips/window. The prior close target frame cut off the bottom of this point.

The bet lower mass is broad and filled. It lacks unique shoulders, separated stamps or a long thin stem. Its difference in bulk from plain-bet controls prevents certifying absence, while the mass does not preserve a unique vowel class.
The thick bet foot/lower block obscures its point structure. A rectangular low edge alone cannot discriminate vowel types or establish absence against natural bet-foot controls.

Below the kaf ordinary bowl are two comparable rounded vertical nodes joined by narrow necks. The same-page kaf in נכבד repeats this sheva shape. The kaf qamats in מכל has a broad shoulder and a long thin stem/button; kaf segol has an added third node and patah a shallow plateau, unlike the target.

The shin has paired low lobes and a central valley/window that match same-letter tsere in חורשי and the first shin of ששת. The second shin of ששת has a substantial third central lower node. Only the vowel is certified; the independent shin-dagesh note remains.
The sin has a large continuous lower base without a complete separately diagnostic stamp arrangement. Same-font shin/sin tsere and segol controls do not uniquely identify this filled lower shape.
